candidates.severity: unassigned; typed identity is flattened before a private transition and reconstructed
candidates.classification: 95e revisit of the same earlier Lens12 contract, not a new unique historical defect.
candidates.trace: seed_case_custody matches typed AssetId and SubjectId objective leaves, flattens each to a raw string plus separate native kind, stores those pairs in a temporary string-keyed map, then passes kind and raw string to private transition_case_custody. That helper reconstructs the existing core CustodyObject before core apply_custody and before final native CaseCustody insertion. The asset and subject record adapters also construct typed fact identities while separately sending raw kind and ID to this private transition. The object is flattened again for actual native storage.
candidates.connected_repair: After the audit carry the existing CustodyObject through private seed and record transitions until the native row boundary. Preserve exact source/party/case/version/holder semantics, generated custody coverage, ordinary and resident NPC dispatch, unattributed initial seeding, terminal transitions, caller guards and transaction behavior. Native inputs still require validated admission.
candidates.discovery: partial; all callers, generated authoring, native transition/retry, aliases and independent lenses open

candidates.severity: unassigned; admitted objective identity is lowered to text before a private comparison and retained tuple
candidates.classification: 95e revisit of the same earlier Lens12 contract, not a new unique historical defect.
candidates.trace: The typed ObjectiveExpression exposes objective.id as an existing ObjectiveId. issue_dialogue_investigation_bindings passes objective.id.as_str() to generated_dialogue_recipient and generated_dialogue_producer_recipient, which compares the string with the typed producer objective_id lowered again. It also stores a string objective ID in temporary matches and pending tuples before inserting DialogueInvestigationBinding.objective_id. The subsequent effect reloads the binding, checks session, character, party, action family, revision, recipient and open case, then finds the objective by this stored ID and rechecks generated producer and custody version. Native binding storage is a real boundary; the earlier private comparison and temporary tuple precede it.
candidates.connected_repair: After the audit retain existing ObjectiveId through private matching and pending structures and encode it at native insertion. Preserve exact observer provenance, action/recipient/revision bindings, manual versus generated case behavior, ambiguity rejection and selected custody guards; trace all producers and consumers.
candidates.discovery: partial; manual and generated producers, participant cardinality, all binding consumers, aliases and independent lenses open

candidates.severity: unassigned; symbolic conflicting private retry can be acknowledged under stated state preconditions
candidates.classification: New bounded 95e admission-contract question; no player-reachable incident or historical unique-count change established.
candidates.trace: When the current CaseCustody row still has the same source ID, transition_case_custody compares case, object kind and ID, holder kind and ID, and version. For Some(fact), it only checks that the paired case outcome fact has the same case and party; it does not compare the supplied fact kind or payload. A symbolic first successful internal record_asset_returned_or_exchanged call with exchange=false and a later call using the same source, case, party, asset, recipient and version but exchange=true meet the row comparison while requesting AssetReturned versus AssetExchanged. If the first paired fact is present with matching case and party and the row still has that source, the second call returns Ok(false) without comparing those meanings. This is a private-API source counterexample, not an executed transaction.
candidates.actual_caller_safeguards: Selected dialogue callers choose Return or Exchange from the current objective, derive the source from session, action and objective, bind the action family and recipient, and require an unconsumed revision and current party-held custody version before invoking the helper. The source search found these two helper calls in dialogue effects; it does not establish an admitted path to conflicting replay. Investigation pickup and capture use different selected transitions and guards. The old same-source row can also be replaced by later transitions, a separate replay-policy question.
candidates.connected_repair: Decide and enforce whether a retry must bind the typed outcome kind and all material coordinates as well as custody attribution. Preserve legitimate exact retries without comparing a newly sampled clock as though it were immutable request data; reconcile all callers and transaction/receipt lifetimes first.
candidates.discovery: partial; reachable retry, durable fact equality, outer receipts, source namespace, time and aliases open

candidates.severity: unassigned; development editor offers objective variants rejected by generated-case validation
candidates.classification: New bounded 95e development-authoring contract assessment; no product execution or historical unique-count change established.
candidates.trace: The development-gated schema advertises PresentProof among objective_requirements and supplies a matching constructor. The editor renders every listed option and replaces the selected draft requirement with its constructor. The spawn route deserializes the draft and calls developer_quest::compile. If earlier checks pass, compile namespaces the definition, builds GeneratedCase and always invokes quest_generation::validate; its per-objective producer match has no PresentProof arm and falls through to false, adding a structural no-concrete-owning-producer error. Thus an otherwise accepted draft containing that leaf cannot be compiled through this path, even with compatibility warnings overridden. Other listed variants also reach the default branch, but this record uses PresentProof as the concrete example and does not claim complete option inventory or an observed browser event.
candidates.safeguards_and_scope: Schema/spawn are development-enabled only and preserve existing structural diagnostics. Generated dialogue producers presently support Expose and ReturnAsset, so presenting physical proof is not a demonstrated supported generated gameplay path. The selected physical evidence projection uses scene evidence while the dialogue proof check demands a same-ID party/character custody row; the validated asset and subject custody prefixes differ from the selected ordinary generator’s evidence: prefix. Generated-case validation rejects PresentProof before materialization, so no normal generated-quest deadlock is claimed from that mismatch. Manual evidence admission and future support remain open.
candidates.connected_repair: Decide which objective kinds the development authoring interface actually supports. Derive its offered options and constructors from the same supported production/validation contract, or implement the missing producers in a separately authorized later change; preserve structural validation, producer/recipient provenance and explicit unsupported behavior.
candidates.discovery: partial; full objective list, manual case support, documentation, all authors and aliases open

bounded_safeguards.question: Can the same validated text be both an Asset and Subject custody identity?
bounded_safeguards.disposition: AssetId::new requires the asset: prefix and SubjectId::new requires subject:. transition_case_custody reconstructs both the requested object and an existing row through these constructors. A single string cannot satisfy both constructors, so this selected validated path does not show an asset/subject same-key collision. Serde admission, malformed persisted rows and same-kind cross-case identifiers remain separate questions; a corrupted kind/ID row can be rejected rather than silently accepted.
bounded_safeguards.qualification: Source-only reasoning, no constructors or database run.
